messages.content:
You draft show-cause notices for a wetlands regulator in West Bengal, India.

You will be given (a) a water-loss event confirmed from satellite data, and
(b) the verbatim text of statutory provisions that were retrieved from the source
instruments for you.

ABSOLUTE RULES:
1. You may cite ONLY the provisions supplied to you, using exactly the citation
   strings given. Do not cite any other rule, section, act, judgment or authority,
   even if you are confident it exists. If a provision you want is not in the list,
   write around its absence.
2. Do not paraphrase a provision as though it were its text. When you state what
   the law requires, quote it.
3. Do not assert any fact that is not in the event data — no ownership, no names,
   no dates of construction, no intent. Where the notice needs a fact you were not
   given, write a bracketed blank like [name of occupier] for the officer to fill.
4. Do not state a conclusion of law. The notice asks the recipient to show cause;
   it does not find them in breach.

Format — plain text, this structure, no markdown:
  reference line, date line
  addressee block
  Subject line
  1. The facts observed (satellite measurement, dates, area)
  2. The provisions engaged (quoted, with citation)
  3. What the recipient is required to do, and by when
  4. Signature block
Keep it under 450 words.

EVENT (confirmed by satellite measurement, not by you)
Pond reference: EKW_00025 (Pond near KA Block)
Mouza: KA Block
Ward / block: Kolkata
Approximate coordinates: 22.559333, 88.401844
Site: East Kolkata Wetlands, Ramsar site no. 1208
Period observed: 2024-11-01 to 2025-11-01
Water surface expected for the season: 4.54 ha
Water surface actually observed: 2.79 ha
Reduction: 38 per cent (1.75 ha)
Seasonal variation already accounted for: yes
Recovered since: no
Surface condition now: Bare earth / fill visible where water was

ADDRESSEE: [name of occupier / owner — unknown]
ISSUING OFFICER: [officer name], [designation]
DATE: 2026-08-28

PROVISIONS RETRIEVED FOR YOU — cite only these:

[Rule 4(2)(i)] — Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017
"(i) conversion for non-wetland uses including encroachment of any kind;"

[Rule 2(1)(i)] — Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017
"(i)    “wise use of wetlands” means maintenance of their ecological character, achieved through implementation
of ecosystem approach within the context of sustainable development;
(j)    “zone of influence” means that part of the catchment area of the wetland or wetland complex,
developmental activities in which induce adverse changes in ecosystem structure, and ecosystem services."

[Rule 4] — Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017
"4.    Restrictions of activities in wetlands.—(1) The wetlands shall be conserved and managed in accordance with the
principle of 'wise use' as determined by the Wetlands Authority."

[Rule 5(4)(d)] — Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017
"(d)     prepare a comprehensive digital inventory of all wetlands within a period of one year from the date of
publication of these rules and upload the same on a dedicated web portal to be developed by the
Central Government for the said purpose; the inventory to be updated every ten years;
(e)     develop a comprehensive list of activities to be regulated and permitted within the notified wetlands
and their zone of influence;
(f)     recommend additions, if any, to the list of prohibited activities for specific wetlands;
(g)     define strategies for conservation and wise use of wetlands within their jurisdiction; wise use being a
principle for managing these ecosystems which incorporates sustainable uses (such as capture
fisheries at subsistence level or harvest of aquatic plants) as being compatible with conservation, if
ecosystem functions (such as water storage, groundwater recharge, flood buffering) and values (such
as recreation and cultural) are maintained or enhanced;
(h)     review integrated management plan for each of the notified wetlands (including trans-boundary
wetlands in coordination with Central Government), and within these plans consider continuation and
support to traditional uses of wetlands which are harmonized with ecological character;"

response:
Memo No: [reference number]
Date: 2026-08-28

To,
[name of occupier / owner — unknown]
[Address]

Subject: Notice to show cause regarding water-loss and surface alteration at pond reference EKW_00025, Mouza: KA Block, Kolkata.

1. The facts observed
Satellite data analysis covering the period from 2024-11-01 to 2025-11-01 for pond reference EKW_00025 (Pond near KA Block), situated in Mouza: KA Block, Kolkata, within the East Kolkata Wetlands (Ramsar site no. 1208), at approximate coordinates 22.559333, 88.401844, indicates the following: the water surface expected for the season was 4.54 ha, whereas the water surface actually observed was 2.79 ha. This represents a reduction of 38 per cent (1.75 ha), with seasonal variation already accounted for. The water-loss has not recovered since, and the surface condition now shows bare earth / fill visible where water was.

2. The provisions engaged
The statutory provisions applicable to the conservation and management of wetlands under the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017 are as follows:

Rule [Rule 4]:
"4.    Restrictions of activities in wetlands.—(1) The wetlands shall be conserved and managed in accordance with the
principle of 'wise use' as determined by the Wetlands Authority."

Rule [Rule 4(2)(i)]:
"(i) conversion for non-wetland uses including encroachment of any kind;"

Rule [Rule 2(1)(i)]:
"(i)    “wise use of wetlands” means maintenance of their ecological character, achieved through implementation
of ecosystem approach within the context of sustainable development;
(j)    “zone of influence” means that part of the catchment area of the wetland or wetland complex,
developmental activities in which induce adverse changes in ecosystem structure, and ecosystem services."

Rule [Rule 5(4)(d)]:
"(d)     prepare a comprehensive digital inventory of all wetlands within a period of one year from the date of
publication of these rules and upload the same on a dedicated web portal to be developed by the
Central Government for the said purpose; the inventory to be updated every ten years;
(e)     develop a comprehensive list of activities to be regulated and permitted within the notified wetlands
and their zone of influence;
(f)     recommend additions, if any, to the list of prohibited activities for specific wetlands;
(g)     define strategies for conservation and wise use of wetlands within their jurisdiction; wise use being a
principle for managing these ecosystems which incorporates sustainable uses (such as capture
fisheries at subsistence level or harvest of aquatic plants) as being compatible with conservation, if
ecosystem functions (such as water storage, groundwater recharge, flood buffering) and values (such
as recreation and cultural) are maintained or enhanced;
(h)     review integrated management plan for each of the notified wetlands (including trans-boundary
wetlands in coordination with Central Government), and within these plans consider continuation and
support to traditional uses of wetlands which are harmonized with ecological character;"

3. What the recipient is required to do, and by when
You are hereby required to show cause in writing, supported by relevant documents, why action should not be taken against you in view of the satellite-observed reduction in water surface and appearance of bare earth / fill at the aforementioned site. Your written explanation must reach the office of the undersigned within [number] days from the date of receipt of this notice.

4. Signature block
[officer name]
[designation]
West Bengal Wetlands Authority
